name: Tai Do-Mene-Yo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog cites only Pittayaporn 2009 (subgrouping) and Ferlus 2008 (historical comment); no grammar/phonology of Tai Yo located

sources.citation: Michaud, Alexis & Frédéric Pain. 2015. ISO 639-3 change request 2015-019 (rename tyj Tai Do -> Tai Yo; merge nyw Tai Nyaw and tmp Tai Mène into tyj).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Identity only: Tai Mène (Laos), Tai Nyo/Nyaw (Nakhon Phanom, Prachin Buri) and Tai Quy Chau are one language; cites Ferlus 1993, 2008, Chamberlain 1991, Nantaporn 1989.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory 'Tay Yo (EA 2582)', contributor D. Nikolaev, source Ferlus 2008.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 34 segments; no suprasegmental/stress statement.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Image-only scan of a conference handout at 75 dpi (no text layer, not scanned — too low resolution); superseded by Ferlus 2008.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology of 'Lao Nyo' of Cambodia (concludes it is Lao, not Nyo/Yo): syllable structure CV:T, CVVT, CVCT etc., 20 consonants, tones; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Pittayaporn, Pittayawat. 2009. The Phonology of Proto-Tai. PhD dissertation, Cornell University (eCommons 1813/13855).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative/reconstructive; stress discussed only for Proto-Tai sesquisyllables (minor unstressed + major stressed syllable) and Siamese word minimality; Nyo (Tha Uthen) cited from Hudak 1997 / Boonsner 1984; no statement on Tai Yo stress.

sources.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 2008. Les dialectes tai du Nghệ An, Vietnam (Tay Daeng, Tay Yo, Tay Muong). French original (2017 version) of the chapter in Diller, Edmondson & Luo (eds), The Tai-Kadai Languages, London: Routledge, 298-315. HAL halshs-01617791.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. p. 3 §3 Généralités phonétiques: 'La structure du mot de base dans les trois dialectes, tay daeng (tay thanh), tay yo et tay muong, est strictement monosyllabique: CV(C)/T'; then initials, vowels (length), six-tone system. Tay Yo section §5 (pp. 8-13): consonants, vowels, tones (DL1/DL2 merger), grammar notes.

sources.citation: Rose, Phil. 1998. Tones of a tridialectal: acoustic and perceptual data on ten linguistic tonetic contrasts between Lao, Nyo and Standard Thai. ICSLP 1998. DOI 10.21437/ICSLP.1998-100.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tone acoustics of one Nyo speaker (Sakon Nakhon); monosyllabic Gedney-list words; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 1993. Phonétique et écriture du Tai de Qui Châu (Vietnam). Cahiers de Linguistique - Asie Orientale 22(1): 87-106. DOI 10.3406/clao.1993.1432.
sources.access_detail: read online, no copy kept
